body.estimand_functional: \(\tau(z_0)=\sum_{s=1}^{S}\pi_s\{\mathbb E[B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}\mid z_0]-m_s(z_{0s})\}\) under consistency and event-date transport.  Conditional on \(z_0\), the donor sample factors from the entire joint panel, so conditioning further on the exact design preserves the donor product experiment and its independence from all unit histories.  For \(0<\lambda\le1\), the separately defined deterministic fixed-design experiment has minimax MSE at most \(CR_{X,\mathrm{opt}}\) for every fixed design and minimax MSE \(\asymp R_{X,\mathrm{opt}}\) when \(\delta_0<1/2\) and \(B^4>(Sd)^2\); every causal law inherits the conditional upper bound for almost every realized design.  The anchor estimator has the computable upper certificate \(R_D\).  Marginally, \(\sup_P\operatorname{MSE}_P(\widehat\tau)\le CR_\star\) over the base Holder class, and the global minimax MSE is \(\asymp R_\star\) under the same donor-support nondegeneracy.  No headline rate assumes a class-wide lower local modulus.

sampling_model.design: For each fixed cohort, \(T\) exact pre-event paths have density bounded above and away from zero.  Conditional analysis is an ordinary minimax problem in the separately defined deterministic experiment \(\mathfrak E_X(z_0,\Sigma)\) for every fixed \(X\); causal conditional kernels enter it for almost every realized design.  The Gram radius certifies an estimator but is never a minimax converse.
sampling_model.units: Each cohort supplies \(n_s\) replicated untreated blocks per calendar window and \(n_s\) treated event outcomes.  Given the exact design and realized path, untreated responses are centered at \(m_s(X_{st})\), treated outcomes retain their path-conditional mean, and histories are independent across units.  Dependence between training responses and the treated event outcome within one unit history remains unrestricted.
sampling_model.treatment: Consistency identifies observed event wealth with treated potential wealth.  Event-date transport separately equates the unobserved untreated event mean with the historical regression at the realized path; neither design-conditional centering nor any local modulus identifies this causal equality.
sampling_model.overlap: Every realized cohort path is at least \(\delta_0\) from the cube boundary.  Exact fixed-design recovery can be easier than an anchor bandwidth suggests when a site equals the realized path.  A nondegenerate donor-location converse requires \(\delta_0<1/2\); at the endpoint the admissible path set can collapse to the cube center.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Only the event path is generated: deterministic donor folds produce projected means, and the full stacked covariance retains all cross-coordinate, cross-horizon, and cross-cohort dependence.  Conditional on the realized path, the donor-score sigma-field is independent of the sigma-field generated jointly by the entire exact-design, untreated-response, and treated-event panel.  Hence conditioning further on the exact design preserves the donor law and donor-versus-unit-history independence.  The upper bounds need only ellipticity and the fourth-moment envelope; the donor lower experiment additionally uses the necessary strict slack \(B^4>(Sd)^2\).

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: The Gaussian convex-class theory relates minimax estimation of a linear functional to a fixed-design modulus of continuity and near-optimal affine recovery.
Theorems 7 and 8 combine local-polynomial estimation with evaluation at an independent estimated minimizer under strong convexity.
Theorem 1 expands local-linear regression when an estimated covariate is attached to every training observation.
Theorems 3.1--3.6 address replicated classical measurement error on every latent training coordinate by deconvolution.
The ordinary random-design Holder benchmark gives the classical multivariate nonparametric regression rate.
Local-linear smoothers attain ordinary pointwise minimax order under regular fixed or random design.
Ordered moduli characterize finite-sample confidence intervals for linear functionals in known Gaussian experiments.
Bias-aware local-polynomial intervals combine a worst-case bias bound with stochastic calibration.
Synthetic-control prediction intervals account for weight estimation and dependent innovations using block methods.
Proposition 3.1 studies factor-loading recovery when controls and pre-treatment periods jointly grow.

body.tldr: The causal target remains cohort-weighted buy-and-hold level wealth at a realized event path, identified only by consistency and the explicitly untestable event-date transport equality.  Conditional on the realized path, the donor sample is now stated explicitly to factor from the entire joint panel; this preserves donor independence from all unit histories after conditioning on the exact design and does not restrict dependence within a unit history.  The base model contains the Holder, centering, mixing, boundedness, and donor-moment conditions but no class-wide lower local modulus.  For \(0<\lambda\le1\), the deterministic fixed-design product experiment, nearest-design estimator, anchor estimator, total interval, and explicit lower witnesses deliver matching conditional, marginal, and honest-length rates.  The nonredundant marginal channels are treated replication, calendar spacing, and donor location; geometric beta mixing incurs \(\{\log(T\vee2)/T\}^{2\lambda/d}\), whereas independent calendars give \(T^{-2\lambda/d}\).  Strict fourth-moment and interior slack are required only for the regular donor converse; exact constants and higher-order signed-weight stability remain open.

project_justification.gap: Classical fixed-point regression does not combine replicated sites with an externally generated query, while a conditional minimax statement at every continuously distributed design is ill posed if it ranges over arbitrary versions of regular conditional laws.  The substantive fixed-design object is the deterministic product-experiment modulus, not Gram invertibility or a class-wide lower direction.
project_justification.niche: Historical market paths may be recorded exactly even when the event-date counterfactual path is synthesized from donors.  This separates realized-site optimal recovery, full-covariance donor-location uncertainty, and the untestable causal transport equality.
project_justification.fill: The note derives the causal observed-law functional, defines a deterministic fixed-design product experiment and its joint modulus, and proves a rough-Holder frontier using explicit treated-mean, distance-function, donor-location, and rare-cluster witnesses.  The donor sample factors from the full joint panel conditional on the realized path, which makes the almost-sure model-to-experiment bridge valid while preserving unrestricted dependence within each unit history.  The lower constructions lie directly in the base Holder class and require no class-wide lower local-modulus condition.  The anchor/extrapolation rule remains a computable upper certificate and attains the corrected marginal and honest-length rates.

body.related_work: Donoho (1994) supplies the classical Gaussian link between a linear-functional modulus and near-minimax affine estimation; the present result derives a bounded-response, rough-Holder product-experiment comparison with a generated full-covariance query.  Stone (1982) and Fan (1993) give ordinary Holder and pointwise local-polynomial benchmarks but not replicated sites plus a generated center.  Mammen, Rothe, and Schienle (2012) perturb every training coordinate, while Delaigle, Hall, and Meister (2008) study classical error in every latent coordinate; neither experiment applies to an exact historical design with only the event center generated.  Akhavan, Gogolashvili, and Tsybakov (2024) study sample-split evaluation at an estimated minimizer, where strong convexity changes the location channel.  Armstrong and Kolesar (2018, 2020) motivate modulus and bias-aware interval calculations, and Cattaneo, Feng, and Titiunik (2021) motivate dependent block calibration.  These sources inform the architecture; the deterministic induced experiment, nearest-site characterization, donor-product combination, and three-channel panel frontier are derived here.
body.interpretation: Conditionally, two exact designs with the same Gram certificate can have different difficulty: an exact site at the event path eliminates spatial recovery error, whereas a nearby hole leaves a Holder-sized ambiguity.  The fixed-design claim is an ordinary deterministic experiment for each design, and the causal transfer holds for almost every realized design because the donor sample factors from the entire joint panel before design conditioning.  Marginally, occupancy converts the ambiguity into the geometric-mixing spacing rate.  Donor uncertainty dominates when \(N^{-\lambda}\) exceeds treated replication and spacing, provided the donor class contains a regular overlapping location subfamily; no regression lower-modulus assumption is involved.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The no-deconvolution conclusion relies on exact historical paths.  The constructive frontier is proved for \(0<\lambda\le1\), where nearest-site and local-constant weights are nonnegative and have unit absolute mass.  For \(\lambda>1\), controlling the conditional stochastic norm of signed higher-order recovery weights remains open.  Geometric beta mixing retains the logarithmic spacing penalty, with a no-log i.i.d. corollary.  The donor lower bound requires \(B^4>(Sd)^2\) and \(\delta_0<1/2\); without this slack the allowed donor experiment can be singular and the root-\(N\) location lower bound need not hold.  Exact phase-intersection constants remain open.
body.honest_scope: Event-date transport is an untestable causal restriction, while design-conditional centering is a distinct observed-law sampling condition.  Donor--panel separation is only a conditional factorization between the donor sample and the complete joint panel; it leaves dependence within every unit's training/event history unrestricted.  All upper-risk, coverage, and expected-length results for \(0<\lambda\le1\) hold on the base Holder class without a class-wide lower local modulus.  The spacing and fixed-design recovery converses need no such modulus.  The donor-location contribution to the MSE and honest-length converses requires the disclosed nondegeneracy \(B^4>(Sd)^2\) and \(\delta_0<1/2\).  Growing dimension, adaptation, uniform-in-path bands, exact constants, and higher-order signed-weight stability remain open.
